## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #227 at **f91b3ffffea45b678dd35a8d9460d4a9e50703a0**, under C33/C34. Reviewed the ten-file delta and traced the registration predicates against the related-row selection. No missing-row counterexample or skipped security refusal identified.

`related_seats` selects the union of claim/supersedes IDs, carried observation/prebind IDs, matching session, pane and PID (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:1513-1530`). Registration queries retain retired rows and other harnesses.

| Predicate family | Why its required rows remain selected |
|---|---|
| Explicit address/foreign session, target and explicit supersession | Named addresses are fetched directly or selected by ID; session/pane fallback candidates remain (`registration.rs:500-513,1389-1406,1533-1553,1602-1644`). |
| F162 holder and implicit predecessor | Explicit predecessor is selected by ID; inferred predecessor necessarily shares current PID/pane. Incarnation/live-native predicates still apply (`523-548,1562-1599,1669-1699`). |
| Observation/prebind revalidation | Carried IDs remain selected even if their other keys changed; ownership is rechecked under lock (`795-830,1647-1656`). |
| Native address and process conflicts | Conflicts necessarily match session, pane or PID. Same-session rows across harnesses and retirement states remain visible; ordinary process equality implies selected PID (`835-853,932-1023,1746-1793`). |
| Retired continuity, owner-close and paneless history | The included target supplies its continuity/tombstone facts; same-session/PID history remains ordered for live/newest-incarnation/ID selection (`894-912,1062-1080,1451-1507`). |
| Spawn predecessor/retirement | Session selection and carried observed/prebind IDs cover these dependencies (`915-929,1220-1276`). |

For a native A-to-B-to-C transition, a retired A retry still selects A by ID/session and current C by PID/pane; an unrelated retired intermediate cannot satisfy the live implicit-predecessor predicate. This is a source trace, not an executed multi-hop proof.

**ID uniqueness:** candidate-by-candidate `get` checks see occupied live and retired IDs outside the related set (`registration.rs:240-255,860-878`). The existing registration mutex spans locked reread through commit (`231-233,795-1308`). This preserves the current serialization boundary; it is not a transactional get-and-reserve allocator or protection against arbitrary writers outside that lock.

SQLite uses the same four bound OR alternatives and ID ordering as the relation; the fake inherits that relation with ordered-map iteration (`crates/core/src/ports.rs:66-99,156-165`; `crates/store/src/registry.rs:460-488`; `crates/testkit/src/fakes.rs:60-64,155-183`). Contract assertions cover each relation, retired rows, negative matches, union/order and live-only exclusion (`testkit/src/contract.rs:175-250`).

The live-only observer/binder/receiver queries omit rows their existing predicates already excluded. Retired tap cleanup still uses tracked panes/world reconciliation, not retired registry rows (`daemon/src/pane_observer.rs:227-320`; `claude_bind.rs:70-79,171-177`; `codex_bind.rs:217-229,335-341`; `delivery/mod.rs:629-663`).
